newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says won't cut reserve requirements.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says won't cut reserve requirements.

text.p: Taiwan's deputy central bank governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Monday the bank had no plans to discuss lowering banks' reserve requirements during its upcoming May 8 board meeting.
"It is not an appropriate time to lower reserve requirements. The central bank has no plans to discuss it during the May 8 board meeting," Hsu told reporters.

On Monday afternoon the overnight interbank rate was at 6.534 percent against Saturday's 6.582 close -- still far outside the central bank's 5.00-5.50 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper at 6.50-6.60 against 6.65.
Some analysts had suspected that the central bank would consider cutting banks' reserve requirements to ease banking system's liquidity.
The central bank, which has tried to cool the island's recent stock market fever, would like to see "appropriate" growth, Hsu said.
Taiwan's stock market had risen more than 25 percent in 1997 alone in what analysts called a liquidity-driven rally.
